Śaka 1430, Vibhava Vaiśākha śu. 15=
1508 A.D., April
15 (the week day being Saturday).
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Pośīpūḍu being a village without water (nilluni pośīpūḍu) in Mūliki-nāḍu as eka-bhōga to Peḍa-Tiṁmamaya son of Kēmaraju of Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Āśvalāyana-sūtra by the king. cells.remarks: Records the gift of income from taxes (maṁgama) on the products like salt, cotton, pepper, etc. for the purpose of daily worship and offerings, perpetual lamp, water-shed, flower garland etc. to the deity Chennarāya of Guḍipāḍu by the merchants of fifty countries including Pṛithvīšēṭi Rāyanama-tiri Bhāskaraṇa and others belonging to Ayyana (governing body) of the merchants. Records the consecration of the deity Gopinatha at Kaṭṭagūru by Ijjikāla Mālseṭi and registers a grant of land and flower garden by him (Mālseṭi), the name of theoy (ippa-pellēvuru) and a servant, the name Elaya Gopaya on the above occasion (Published in H.A.S., No. 19, km. 5)

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH / CUDDAPAH DISTRICT / PRODDATUR TALUK · Khaṭakūr † — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: Second side of the same slab (Salar Jung Museum) †
cells.remarks: Refers to the king as Mahāmāṇḍaleśvara and refers to a grant of land for the purpose of worship of the deity in the temple of the 18 communities, including the mahājanaas, the nagara, the kāmpus and the bālanješeṭṭis, of the place Kaṭṭagūru for the merit of the king. Also states that they remitted the income from taxes, from the fields yielding two crops in a year, to the cultivators of summer crops, namely, māru, śaradyāru for one kār crop at the rate of one māḍa of gold. At the end of the record details of arrangements made for the protection (kāmpupeṭṭu) of the different vṛittis are specified. (Ibid. [Published in H.A.S., No. 19, Km. 5.], Km. 5.)

cells.place: Bar lying on the bank of Kaṭajam-mācheguvu.
cells.date: Śaka 1164 (mistake for 1162), Sarvarī, Vaiśākha [Ni]ja-Vaiśākha śu. 3, Thursday=1240 A.D., April 26.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of a vṛtti of two marturus of land with two seasonal crops (māgaṇa-bhaumi) in front of [māga-vāṇa] of the sluice canal behind Bollasamudram, for the deity Mūlāsthāna Prōlakamma of Koṇḍapalli by the Rēcherla chief Pādyūru Gaṇapati-rāḍḍi. The Telugu portion is in verse and corrupt. The Sanskrit prose is in prose. Further, it registers the gift of jewels, articles of worship, 20 cows (mōdālu) for the lamp and rice, for the daily food-offerings to the deities Prōlakamma, Nūnamamma and Mārkamma by the nīyōga-bhōya. Provision was made for the nīyōga-bhoja of Cheliadēvata. The record was engraved by Mappadōju.

cells.remarks: Refers to mahāsāmanta piriya-bēṇeyya Peṇpu-rāvuṭa and states that at the command of daṇḍanāyaka Śivarāja, a grant of land was made to god Peṇpēśvaradēva for the aṅgarogabhoga of the deity and for feeding the ascetics and students therein. cells.date: Sarvadhāri, Puşya śu.13, Sunday = 1108 A.D., December 20 (the week day being Friday).
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land by Iśvarava-daṇḍāyaka who was the brother of mahāpradhāna Sōvarasa-daṇḍāyaka for the offerings and repairs (khaṇḍasphuțita-jīrṇōdhāra) in the temple of the deity Hulliyamēśvara. A few more grants were made by various persons to the same god.

cells.location: GULBARGA DISTRICT / SINDHANOOR TALUK · Sālagunda — Karnataka
cells.place: Stone buried near the well of Jakkanma. Inscription No. 1.
cells.remarks: Narrates the genealogy of the king starting from Niramṇadi Taila down to Vikramāditya VI. Eulogizes the race of Nāgaṇeva, who was the feudatory of the king. States that the Bāchiga who hailed from Nāga race was administering the village, Sāgulunda; describes abrahamaṇya of Someśvara and the grant of lands to the god Someśvara at Sāgalaṇḍa; registers the gift of land on sōma Nāgadēva 43 dagadhāśa; registers the gift of land of one kandan, near the bank of Tuńgabhadrā river, to the god Nāgēśvaradēva at Sālagunda, for the arga-bhōga, chatra, samā(dhi) yoga, aśana, dīpa, tṛīha etc. Further, records gifts of land made by an assembly of 20 (mahājanas) who are also referred to as its protectors.

cells.location: ORISSA / PURI DISTRICT / BHUBANESWAR TAHSIL · Maṇḍalgaṛh † — Odisha
cells.place: Broken slab lying on the bank of a tank.
cells.date: Vikrama 1852, Śrāvaṇa śu. 15, Friday = 1795 A.D., July 31.
cells.remarks: Refers to tank (tālāka) at Maṇḍalagaṛh (on the bank of which, the described slab is lying) and the same (kāku) temple is also situated on the same bank. The mādh was performed on the orders of (ādeśa) mahārājādhirāja, mahā-rāja Bhīmasiṁha. Namenitioned Mēhuta Vēcharadāsa and Chhitarāma, etc. It records that at the end of every lunar month verses at the end which state that a Hindu does not harm to this he will eat cow's flesh and a Muslim the Pig's (Suvara) meat.

cells.location: ORISSA / KAMARAJAR DISTRICT VIRUDHUNAGAR TALUK · KAMARAJAR DISTRICT VIRUDHUNAGAR TALUK Sengunäpuram — Odisha
cells.place: Siva temple, central shrine, adhisthāna, jagati and kumuda, south and west faces.
cells.remarks: Begins with the prasasti Prthvikänta-śri, etc., of the king. Records gift for the perpetual burning of a nandasēvi-dīpam and for the daily offerings to the deity of Ammanḍai of Śri Kayilāsam alias Näpattenṇāyir-Īśvaram-Udaiyār at Sengunäpuram alias Abinävapuramangaram in Sengunä-nādu. The old dēvadāna villages of the deity Korgaṇeri and Sendarāneri have been excluded as they have been set apart to meet the royal tax. The oral order (tiruvāykēl) of the king was conveyed to the pantāram mülappäduppandāriya-dēvakarmis and the Srīmahēśvarakanmiyäs of the temple by Sivallavabhaṭṭan alias Pāndyāryan and the order was caused to be engraved in the temple. Arayan Irāman alias Visäyiyaräyan of Kāliyan, Sri Vayiravan alias Irāmayan, and Sri Vayirugan Sūtri alias Teunavaräyan of Tachcha-Ne(mmāli in Milaik-küram figure as signatories, who attested the order. In characters of about the 12th century A.D.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / WANDIWASH TALUK · NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT. WANDIWASH TALUK. Sīyamaṅgalam — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Rock-cut Śiva temple, natural rock inside the outer enclosure, southern side.
cells.remarks: This verse inscription is in Śanda Viruttappā metre. It extols a certain Ammai Appaṉ, Kiḷivai Atigamāṉ, by comparing him with Pāri, a chieftain of the Saṅgam age, for the following munificent gifts to the deity enshrined in the temple (Dhanmīchcharam) at Śīyamaṅgalam. These gifts are: 1. the creation of a street (tiruvīdi) around the hill in which the temple is situated for the purpose of taking the temple elephant in procession, 2. the institution of a flower garden (nandavanam), 3. the building of a tower (gōpuram), 4. the excavation of a tank (vāvi), 5. the construction of a sluice (maḍagu) to it and 6. the construction of an enclosure wall (madiḷ-tiruveḍuttukkaṭṭi). In characters of the 13th century A.D.

cells.location: TIRUCHCHIRAPALLI DISTRICT · TIRUCHCHIRAPALLI DISTRICT † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Kumuda of the front maṇḍapa (north face).
cells.remarks: Refers to an agreement entered into the ūrom of Aḷindiyūr in Kō-nāḍu according to which they agreed to measure five kalams of paddy from the cultivated lands in the village to Perumāḷ-uḍaiyār. It is stated that the king was pleased to pay the value for the crops like seasamum, millet, etc., raised therein. Further it is stated that the above lands were made over to the deity Varavapūram-uḍaiya nāyaṉār, as kuḍiṅgai-dēvadāṉam. A number of signatories are associated with the documents. In characters of about the 13th century A.D.

cells.date:
(1) A.H. 966=1558 A.D., October 14-1559 A.D., October 2.

(2) A.H. 1403=1982 A.D., October 19,-1983 A.D., October 7
cells.remarks: Modern. States that the grave is that of Hadrat Shāh Ahmad Jamāl who came to India from Mecca and settled in the region (iqlim) of Bangāla (i.e. Bengal) and devoted himself to religious pursuits. When going to Delhi, he arrived in Bhitri and stayed there. When emperor Akbar came to this territory on the first date he presented himself before the saint and got the blessings. His grave was built in the second date by Muhammad Mas'ūd Shāh, a descendant of the saint. The tablet was inscribed by Yunus, a resident of Lāl Kunwā of Delhi.
